label: Wear OS watch face and companion

map.subsystem: Wear OS watch face and companion (`:watchface` WFF APK, `:wear-device` watch services, phone-side `com.glycemicgpt.mobile.wear` bridge)

capabilities.name: Architecture: single phone app + watch-side services (no separate companion phone app)
capabilities.behavior: Three Gradle modules. (1) `:app` (phone, minSdk 26 / targetSdk 35, applicationId `com.glycemicgpt.mobile`, debug suffix `.debug`) owns all watch management UI, WearDataSender, WatchFacePusher, WearApkPusher, WearChatRelayService, WearMonitoringStatusForwarder. (2) `:wear-device` (watch, namespace `com.glycemicgpt.weardevice`, compileSdk 35 / minSdk 35 / targetSdk 35) — WearableListenerService, 5 complication providers, 3 activities, WatchFacePushManager wrapper, PackageInstaller self-update receiver. (3) `:watchface` (WFF resource-only APK, `hasCode="false"`, minSdk 33 / targetSdk 35, WFF format version 2). CRITICAL HARD CONSTRAINT documented in docs/dev/wear-os-architecture.md:60-64: `:wear-device` MUST declare `applicationId = "com.glycemicgpt.mobile"` — identical to `:app` — because the Wearable Data Layer routes DataClient/MessageClient traffic by applicationId. A mismatch causes silent message drops (`WearableService: Failed to deliver message to AppKey[...]`), discovered during Story 32.8 E2E testing. Only the `namespace` (R class package) differs. Version codes for both wear modules are computed `major*1_000_000 + minor*10_000 + patch` from version 0.14.0 → 140000. EXPLICIT REJECTED ALTERNATIVE (doc lines 12-20): a separate 'wear companion' phone app was considered and rejected — inter-app IPC complexity, two phone apps to manage, two distribution artifacts, no technical benefit. The old `apps/mobile/wear/` module (with HomeActivity, IoBDetailActivity, STT ChatActivity) was REMOVED in Story 32.9; HomeActivity replaced by phone Settings > Watch, IoBDetailActivity removed (IoB detail is now a complication tap action).
edge_cases: Wear OS 6 (API 36) is required at runtime for Watch Face Push; the `watchface-push` AAR's minSdk 36 is overridden via `<uses-sdk tools:overrideLibrary="androidx.wear.watchface.push" />` so the module still builds/runs at minSdk 35. All WatchFacePushManager references are isolated in `@RequiresApi(36)` private methods to prevent class-loading failure on API 35.
On API 35 (Wear OS 5): data listener + complications work normally; `WatchFaceInstaller.isSupported()` returns false and the face must be sideloaded via ADB.

capabilities.name: Wearable Data Layer contract (WearDataContract) — mirrored verbatim in both modules
capabilities.behavior:
Two byte-identical copies (except the phone copy adds `dataUri()`), each with a `// MIRROR:` header pointing at the other. Unit tests on both sides pin every string.

DataClient paths (phone→watch, persistent, all sent with `.setUrgent()`):
  `/glycemicgpt/iob` — keys `iob` (Float), `iob_ts` (Long)
  `/glycemicgpt/cgm` — keys `cgm_mgdl` (Int, raw mg/dL), `cgm_trend` (String), `cgm_ts` (Long), `glucose_unit` (String "mgdl"|"mmol"), `glucose_low`, `glucose_high`, `glucose_urg_low`, `glucose_urg_high` (all Int mg/dL)
  `/glycemicgpt/alert` — keys `alert_type` (String), `alert_bg` (Int), `alert_ts` (Long), `alert_msg` (String), `alert_rebuzz` (Boolean)
  `/glycemicgpt/monitoring_status` — keys `mon_state`, `mon_reason`, `mon_timeout_ms` (Long)
  `/glycemicgpt/history/basal`, `/glycemicgpt/history/bolus`, `/glycemicgpt/history/iob` — keys `history_data` (ByteArray), `history_count` (Int)
  `/glycemicgpt/watchface/config` — keys `cfg_show_iob`, `cfg_show_graph`, `cfg_show_alert`, `cfg_show_seconds` (Bool), `cfg_graph_range_h` (Int), `cfg_theme` (String), `cfg_show_basal`, `cfg_show_bolus`, `cfg_show_iob_ovl`, `cfg_show_modes`, `cfg_ai_tts` (Bool), `cfg_ai_tts_voice` (String)
  `/glycemicgpt/category_labels` — key `cat_labels_json` (JSON object string)

DataClient path (watch→phone): `/glycemicgpt/watch/version` — keys `watch_ver_name` (String), `watch_ver_code` (Int), `watch_update_ch` (String "dev"|"stable"), `watch_dev_build` (Int).

MessageClient paths: `/glycemicgpt/chat/request` (watch→phone, UTF-8 plain text), `/glycemicgpt/chat/response` (phone→watch, JSON `{response, disclaimer}`), `/glycemicgpt/chat/error` (phone→watch, UTF-8 plain text), `/glycemicgpt/alert/dismiss` (watch→phone, EMPTY byte array), `/glycemicgpt/watchface/status` (watch→phone, key=value lines), `/glycemicgpt/watch/apk/status` (watch→phone, key=value lines).

ChannelClient paths (phone→watch, bulk): `/glycemicgpt/watchface/push`, `/glycemicgpt/watch/apk/push`.

Capabilities (declared via `res/values/wear.xml` `android_wear_capabilities` string-array): phone advertises `glycemicgpt_chat_relay`; watch advertises `glycemicgpt_watch_app`.

DEDUPLICATION WORKAROUND (load-bearing): the Wearable Data Layer silently drops a `putDataItem` whose DataMap is byte-identical to the current one. Every sender that must re-deliver unchanged values injects a synthetic key `"_ts"` = `System.currentTimeMillis()` (Long) into the DataMap. Used on IOB, CGM, MONITORING_STATUS, all three history paths, CATEGORY_LABELS, and CONFIG. Deliberately NOT used on ALERT_PATH (alert payloads always differ by timestamp).

Theme value tokens (must match WFF UserConfiguration values): `dark`, `clinical_blue`, `high_contrast`.

`WearDataContract.dataUri(path)` = `Uri.parse("wear://*" + path)` — used by the phone to query DataItems across all nodes.
edge_cases: The watch manifest registers DATA_CHANGED with `pathPrefix="/glycemicgpt/"` (all data paths) but MESSAGE_RECEIVED with `pathPrefix="/glycemicgpt/chat/"` only — the watch never receives non-chat messages.

The phone manifest registers MESSAGE_RECEIVED for `pathPrefix="/glycemicgpt/chat/"` and exact `path="/glycemicgpt/alert/dismiss"` only. GAP: `/glycemicgpt/watchface/status` and `/glycemicgpt/watch/apk/status` messages are sent by the watch but have NO phone-side listener registered and no phone code references them. Install status is effectively write-only today (the architecture doc says 'Story 32.4 will add real-time status listening'; WatchFacePusher's KDoc repeats this).

capabilities.name: Phone→watch data streaming (WearDataSender)
capabilities.behavior:
`@Singleton WearDataSender` with a lazily-created `Wearable.getDataClient(context)`. Every method builds a `PutDataMapRequest`, calls `.asPutDataRequest().setUrgent()`, awaits `putDataItem`, and swallows exceptions with a Timber warning (no retry, no queue) — a disconnected watch is a no-op. Newer methods (`sendMonitoringStatus`, the three history senders, `sendCategoryLabels`, `sendWatchFaceConfig`) rethrow `CancellationException` before the generic catch; the three oldest (`sendIoB`, `sendCgm`, `sendAlert`) catch bare `Exception` and swallow cancellation too.

Methods: `sendIoB(iob: Float, timestampMs)`; `sendCgm(mgDl, trend, timestampMs, low, high, urgentLow, urgentHigh, unit: GlucoseUnit)`; `sendAlert(type, bgValue, timestampMs, message, rebuzz = true)`; `clearAlert()` = `sendAlert(type="none", bgValue=0, timestampMs=now, message="")` with default rebuzz=true; `sendMonitoringStatus(state, reason?, statusTimeoutMs)`; `sendBasalHistory/sendBolusHistory/sendIoBHistory(data: ByteArray, count: Int)`; `sendCategoryLabels(Map<String,String>)` serialized via `JSONObject(labels).toString()`; `sendWatchFaceConfig(...12 params...)`.

Call sites: `PumpPollingOrchestrator.pollIoB()` (fast loop, every 15 s — `INTERVAL_FAST_MS = 15_000L`), `PumpPollingOrchestrator.processCgmReading()` (per CGM reading), `PumpPollingOrchestrator.sendWatchHistoryOverlays()` (slow loop, every 300 s — `INTERVAL_SLOW_MS = 300_000L`), `SettingsViewModel.syncWatchFaceConfig()` (on every config change AND on `checkWatchStatus()` when a nearby node with the app is found), `AiChatViewModel.syncWatchConfig()` (on TTS toggle / voice select).
edge_cases: The unit token rides on CGM_PATH, not the config payload, deliberately: the wire value stays canonical mg/dL and only the rendered/spoken number converts.

No offline queue — data missed while the watch is disconnected is only recovered by (a) the DataLayer's own last-item cache, read at watch app startup by `bootstrapDataFromDataLayer()`, and (b) the watch's SharedPreferences cache.

capabilities.name: Watch-side data receipt & fan-out (GlycemicDataListenerService)
capabilities.behavior:
`WearableListenerService` (not Hilt). `onDataChanged(DataEventBuffer)` filters to `DataEvent.TYPE_CHANGED` and runs TWO PASSES so config/category-labels are applied before data/alert events in the same batch (so `showAlert`/`showIoB` gates see the newest values).

Pass 1: CONFIG_PATH → `WatchDataRepository.updateWatchFaceConfig(...)` with defaults showIoB=true, showGraph=true, showAlert=true, showSeconds=false, graphRangeHours=3, theme="dark", showBasal/showBolus/showIoBOverlay/showModes=true, aiTts=false, aiTtsVoice="". CATEGORY_LABELS_PATH → JSON parsed to Map; parse failure returns null and the update is skipped; blank JSON → empty map.

Pass 2:
- BASAL_HISTORY: requires `data != null && count in 0..500` (MAX_HISTORY_RECORDS=500), decodes, then filters `timestampMs > 0 && rate in 0f..15f` (MAX_BASAL_RATE=15 U/hr, 'hard cap per Tandem pump safety limits'), and `activityMode.coerceIn(0,2)`.
- BOLUS_HISTORY: same count gate; filters `timestampMs > 0 && units/correctionUnits/mealUnits each in 0f..25f` (MAX_BOLUS_UNITS=25 U, 'max single bolus 25U per Tandem safety limits').
- IOB_HISTORY: same count gate; filters `timestampMs > 0 && iob >= 0f`.
- IOB_PATH → `updateIoB(getFloat(iob), getLong(iob_ts))` (no validation).
- CGM_PATH → applies the unit FIRST (`getString(glucose_unit)?.let { updateGlucoseUnit(GlucoseUnit.fromWire(it)) }` — skipped entirely when the key is absent so an older phone build can't reset it), then `isValidGlucose(mgDl)`; invalid values are logged and the whole event is skipped (`return@forEach`). Thresholds go through `sanitizeThresholds` with fallback defaults low=70, high=180, urgentLow=55, urgentHigh=250; trend defaults to "UNKNOWN".
- MONITORING_STATUS_PATH → `state` must be in the 3-value VALID_MONITORING_STATES set or it's rejected with a warning. `timeoutMs` defaults to `WatchFreshness.DEFAULT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS` (=6 min) and is CLAMPED to `10_000L .. 1_800_000L` (MIN 10 s covers the compressed 20 s debug policy; MAX 30 min stops a corrupt payload letting a dead phone look covered for hours). `receivedAtMs = System.currentTimeMillis()` (watch clock).
- ALERT_PATH → `alert_type` default "none"; `rawBg` sanitized to 0 when `!isValidGlucose(rawBg)`; `rebuzz` defaults to TRUE (so an older phone build that only sends on type change still buzzes). Repository is updated ALWAYS; vibration fires only when `type != "none" (ignoreCase) && config.showAlert && rebuzz`.

Complication fan-out (deduped into a `mutableSetOf<Class<*>>`, each provider requested at most once via `ComplicationDataSourceUpdateRequester.requestUpdateAll()`):
- configUpdated → IoB + Graph + Alerts immediately, and sets `lastIoBUpdateMs = lastGraphUpdateMs = now` so throttled paths don't double-fire.
- iobUpdated → IoB if `now - lastIoBUpdateMs >= 60_000L` (IOB_UPDATE_THROTTLE_MS).
- cgmUpdated → BG if `now - lastBgUpdateMs >= 30_000L` (BG_UPDATE_THROTTLE_MS); Graph if `now - lastGraphUpdateMs >= effectiveThrottle`, where effectiveThrottle = `15_000L` when `cgmHistory.size < 10` else `120_000L` (GRAPH_UPDATE_THROTTLE_MS) — a fast bootstrap window while the sparkline is filling.
- historyUpdated → Graph IMMEDIATELY (no throttle) 'backfill data should render immediately', and resets lastGraphUpdateMs.
- alertUpdated → Alerts ALWAYS, unthrottled ('alerts are safety-critical').
- monitoringStatusUpdated → Alerts always, plus BG and IoB subject to their normal throttles. The phone's status heartbeat (≥ every timeout/2) is DELIBERATELY doubling as the periodic re-render tick that lets BG/IoB staleness de-emphasis take effect without a watch-side alarm clock.
- categoryLabelsUpdated → Graph subject to the same effectiveThrottle rule.

`onMessageReceived` handles CHAT_RESPONSE_PATH (null data → `setChatError("Empty response")`; JSON parsed with `optString`; blank `response` → `setChatError("Empty response from AI")`; parse exception → `setChatError("Failed to parse response")`) and CHAT_ERROR_PATH (null → "Unknown error"; text truncated to MAX_ERROR_LENGTH=200 chars plus "..." to avoid rendering stack traces).

Vibration: urgent types (`startsWith("urgent", ignoreCase)`) → `VibrationEffect.createWaveform(longArrayOf(0, 500, 200, 500), -1)` (no repeat); non-urgent → `createOneShot(300, DEFAULT_AMPLITUDE)`. Wrapped in try/catch.
edge_cases: Throttle state (`lastBgUpdateMs`, `lastIoBUpdateMs`, `lastGraphUpdateMs`) is `@Volatile` instance state on the service — it resets whenever the system recreates the WearableListenerService, so the first event after a service restart always passes the throttle.
A CGM event with a valid unit token but an invalid mg/dL still applies the unit change before rejecting the reading (deliberate: the unit is account-global).

capabilities.name: Watch-side state store (WatchDataRepository) with SharedPreferences persistence
capabilities.behavior:
A process-global Kotlin `object` (not injected) exposing `StateFlow`s: `iob: IoBState?`, `cgm: CgmState?`, `cgmHistory: List<CgmState>`, `basalHistory`, `bolusHistory`, `iobHistory`, `alert: AlertState?`, `monitoringStatus: MonitoringStatusState?`, `chatState: ChatState`, `categoryLabels: Map<String,String>`, `watchFaceConfig: WatchFaceConfigState`, `glucoseUnit: GlucoseUnit`.

`init(context)` is `@Synchronized` and idempotent (returns early if prefs already set); opens SharedPreferences file `watch_data_cache` (MODE_PRIVATE) and restores CGM history, current CGM, current IoB, and glucose unit if not already populated.

CGM history buffer: MAX_CGM_HISTORY = 72 entries ('6 hours at 5-min intervals'). `updateCgm` appends atomically via `_cgmHistory.update {}` with a DEDUP_WINDOW_MS = 30_000L rule: a new reading whose |Δtimestamp| < 30 s from ANY existing entry is dropped entirely. Overflow drops from the front (`updated.drop(updated.size - 72)`).

Persistence format (hand-rolled string concat 'for minimal overhead on every 15s update', no JSON):
- CGM history: records joined by `;`, fields by `,` in order `ts,mgDl,trend,low,high,uLow,uHigh`. Restore requires ≥7 parts per record, drops malformed records, takes the last 72; any exception wipes the key.
- Current CGM: same 7-field CSV, single record.
- Current IoB: `"iob,timestampMs"`.
- Glucose unit: the wire token (`mgdl`/`mmol`).
Basal/bolus/IoB history, alert, monitoring status, chat, category labels and config are NOT persisted.

`updateAlert(type, ...)` sets `_alert` to null when `type == "none"` (exact match, case-sensitive) else to an AlertState.

`updateWatchFaceConfig` VALIDATES: `graphRangeHours` must be in `setOf(1,3,6)` else falls back to 3; `theme` must be in `setOf("dark","clinical_blue","high_contrast")` else falls back to "dark".

`updateGlucoseUnit(unit)` early-returns when unchanged, otherwise persists.

Monitoring status is DELIBERATELY NOT PERSISTED (documented): after a watch process restart coverage is genuinely unknown, and the fail-closed 'no recent data' render is the honest one until the phone's next heartbeat (at most timeout/2 away when alive).

`coverageFrom(status, nowMs): WristCoverage` is the pure decay decision:
  - `status == null` → `NoRecentStatus`
  - `ageMs = nowMs - status.receivedAtMs`; if `ageMs < -60_000L` (`WatchFreshness.STATUS_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS`) OR `ageMs >= status.timeoutMs` → `NoRecentStatus`
  - state `server_active` or `floor_watching` → `Watching`
  - state `not_watching` → `NotWatching(reason)`
  - any unknown state string → `NoRecentStatus` (fail-closed)
Boundary pairs pinned by tests: age `timeoutMs-1` → Watching, age `timeoutMs` → NoRecentStatus; receivedAt `now+60_000` → Watching, `now+60_001` → NoRecentStatus.
edge_cases: `BolusHistoryRecord.category` exists with default "" but the wire format carries no category field, so the decoder never populates it — the `categoryLabels[record.category]` lookup in GraphDetailActivity is effectively `categoryLabels[""]` and is dead unless the phone sends an empty-string key.
Because the repository is a process-global object with no reset in production, `AlertsHonestyUiTest` must call `clearAlert()` + `clearMonitoringStatus()` between tests.
Persistence writes use `apply()` (async) — a hard process kill immediately after a CGM push can lose the newest entry.

capabilities.name: Cold-start bootstrap (GlycemicWearDeviceApp)
capabilities.behavior:
`@HiltAndroidApp Application`. `onCreate()`: plants `Timber.DebugTree()` in debug builds, calls `WatchDataRepository.init(this)` FIRST (so complication providers see restored data immediately on cold start), then `bootstrapDataFromDataLayer()` and `publishVersion()` — each on its own `CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.IO)`.

`bootstrapDataFromDataLayer()` reads `Wearable.getDataClient(...).dataItems.await()` (the DataLayer's cached last items) and replays IOB_PATH, CGM_PATH and ALERT_PATH into the repository, applying the same validation as the live listener (unit token applied only if the key is present; `isValidGlucose` rejection; `sanitizeThresholds` with 70/180/55/250 defaults). The `DataItemBuffer` is `release()`d in a `finally`. NOTE: alert bootstrap does NOT sanitize `alert_bg` through `isValidGlucose` (unlike the live path) and does not vibrate.

`publishVersion()` → `WatchVersionPublisher.publish()` puts `/glycemicgpt/watch/version` with `BuildConfig.VERSION_NAME`, `VERSION_CODE`, `UPDATE_CHANNEL` ("dev" for debug, "stable" for release) and `DEV_BUILD_NUMBER` (`-PdevBuildNumber`, 0 in release), `.setUrgent()`.
edge_cases: Complication services can be invoked in a fresh process BEFORE Application.onCreate completes — BgComplicationDataSource, AlertsComplicationDataSource and GraphComplicationDataSource each defensively call `WatchDataRepository.init(applicationContext)`. IoBComplicationDataSource does NOT call init, so on a cold complication-only process it can read an un-restored (null) IoB and render "--".

capabilities.name: Complication provider: BG (blood glucose)
capabilities.behavior:
`BgComplicationDataSource : SuspendingComplicationDataSourceService`. Manifest: SUPPORTED_TYPES `SHORT_TEXT,LONG_TEXT`, UPDATE_PERIOD_SECONDS **300** (documented: 300 s is the platform minimum period; the periodic tick is required so renders age-decay WITHOUT a phone push — 'a push-only complication would freeze its last (reassuring) state forever').

Pure `render(cgmState, nowMs, unit): BgRender` (unit-tested, takes NO coverage input — structural proof that staleness de-emphasis is independent of the 'watching' claim):
  - `valid = cgmState?.takeIf { isValidGlucose(it.mgDl) }`
  - `tier = WatchFreshness.cgmTier(nowMs - timestampMs)`
  - Show the value only for FRESH or STALE; STALE appends a `"?"` marker.
  - FRESH: shortText `"120 →"`, longText `"BG: 120 mg/dL →"`, description `"Blood Glucose: 120 mg/dL"`.
  - STALE (age ≥ 6 min): shortText `"120? →"`, description ends `"(stale)"`.
  - TOO_STALE (age ≥ 15 min) or invalid or null: shortText `"--"`, longText `"BG: --"`, description `"No recent data"`. `ageReferenceMs` is still the reading timestamp when a reading exists ('the age is the only honest thing left to show'); null only when there is no reading at all.

The complication TITLE is a `TimeDifferenceComplicationText` (style `SHORT_SINGLE_UNIT`, `CountUpTimeReference(Instant.ofEpochMilli(ageReferenceMs))`, `setMinimumTimeUnit(TimeUnit.MINUTES)`) so the system updates the 'Xm ago' text without waking the service; falls back to plain `"BG"` when there is no reading.

Preview data uses PREVIEW_MG_DL = 120 rendered in the user's configured unit (calls `init` first).

Trend symbols (`GlucoseDisplayUtils.trendSymbol`): DOUBLE_UP `⇈` (U+21C8), SINGLE_UP `↑`, FORTY_FIVE_UP `↗`, FLAT `→`, FORTY_FIVE_DOWN `↘`, SINGLE_DOWN `↓`, DOUBLE_DOWN `⇊` (U+21CA), anything else `?`.
edge_cases: Boundary pairs pinned by test: age 6min−1ms → "120 →"; age 6min → "120? →"; age 15min−1ms → "120? →"; age 15min → "--".
Future-dated reading (age −5 s) renders FRESH — routine skew is a display concern.
mgDl=900 renders "--" regardless of age.
BG complication is NOT gated by any config toggle (unlike IoB/Graph).

capabilities.name: Complication provider: IoB (insulin on board)
capabilities.behavior:
`IoBComplicationDataSource : SuspendingComplicationDataSourceService`. Manifest: SUPPORTED_TYPES `SHORT_TEXT,LONG_TEXT`, UPDATE_PERIOD_SECONDS 300. Returns `NoDataComplicationData()` immediately when `watchFaceConfig.showIoB == false`.

Pure `render(iobState, nowMs): IoBRender` using the PUMP freshness policy:
  - FRESH (age < 15 min): text `"%.2f".format(iob)` e.g. `"2.45"`, description `"Insulin on Board: 2.45 units"`.
  - STALE (15 min ≤ age < 60 min): text `"2.45?"`, description `"Insulin on Board: 2.45 units (stale)"`.
  - TOO_STALE (age ≥ 60 min) or null: text `"--"`, description `"No recent data"`.
Documented rationale: 'IoB decays fast enough that an hour-old value presented as current is dosing-relevant misinformation… never an unbounded render.'

Title is always plain `"IoB"`. LONG_TEXT renders `"IoB: <text> units"`. Preview shows `"2.45"` / `"Insulin on Board: 2.45 units"`.
edge_cases: Does NOT call `WatchDataRepository.init(applicationContext)` — a cold complication-only process may render "--" until the Application class runs.
IoB value is never validated against a range; only aged.
LONG_TEXT for a STALE value produces "IoB: 2.45? units".

capabilities.name: Complication provider: glucose graph (on-watch sparkline renderer)
capabilities.behavior:
`GraphComplicationDataSource : SuspendingComplicationDataSourceService`. Manifest: SUPPORTED_TYPES `SMALL_IMAGE`, UPDATE_PERIOD_SECONDS **0** (no periodic tick — data-driven only). Returns NoData for any non-SMALL_IMAGE type, when `config.showGraph == false`, when `cgmHistory.size < MIN_READINGS (3)`, or when fewer than 3 readings survive the range cutoff.

Windowing: `rangeMs = config.graphRangeHours * 3_600_000L`; `cutoff = now - rangeMs`; readings filtered `>= cutoff` and sorted by timestamp. `low`/`high` come from the LAST reading in the window. Basal history is loaded (filtered to the same cutoff) only when `showBasalOverlay || showModeBands`; IoB history only when `showIoBOverlay`; **bolus history is hardcoded to `emptyList()` and `showBolusMarkers` hardcoded to `false` — 'too small at 400x100'** (the config toggle only affects the full-screen GraphDetailActivity).

Bitmap caching: `Objects.hash(readings, basalHistory-or-null, iobHistory-or-null, graphConfig, low, high)` compared against `cachedDataHash`; only re-renders on change. Cache is instance state on the service.

Tap action: `PendingIntent.getActivity(..., requestCode 2000, Intent(GraphDetailActivity) with FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK|FLAG_ACTIVITY_CLEAR_TOP, FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT|FLAG_IMMUTABLE)`. Content description: `"Glucose trend: N readings over Hh"`.

**WatchGraphRenderer** (`android.graphics.Canvas` into a 400×100 ARGB_8888 bitmap, PADDING 4f on all sides). Draw order is fixed:
 1. Mode bands (full height, only if `showModeBands` and basal non-empty): sleep `0x0F7E57C2` (purple, 0.06 alpha), exercise `0x0FFF9800` (orange, 0.06 alpha); `activityMode==0` (NONE) skipped; each band spans from its own x to the NEXT record's x (or graphRight for the last), x-clamped to the graph rect, drawn only if `x2 > x1`.
 2. Target-range band: filled rect between `yPos(high)` and `yPos(low)`, color `0x1F22C55E` (green, 0.12 alpha).
 3. Threshold dashed lines at low and high: color `0x80FFFFFF`, strokeWidth 0.5f, `DashPathEffect(floatArrayOf(4f,4f), 0f)`.
 4. Basal stepped area (bottom 15 px, `BASAL_AREA_HEIGHT=15f`): `maxRate = max(rate).coerceAtLeast(0.1f)`; bar height `(rate/maxRate)*15f`; fill alpha 38 (~0.15); top-edge stroke alpha 153 (0.6), 1px; vertical step line at rate changes (|Δy| > 0.5f) alpha 102 (0.4). Colors by `basalColor(isAutomated, activityMode)`: activityMode 1 → `0xFF7E57C2` purple (sleep), 2 → `0xFFFF9800` orange (exercise), else automated → `0xFF00BCD4` teal, else `0xFF78909C` blue-grey.
 5. IoB overlay (bottom 20 px, `IOB_AREA_HEIGHT=20f`): `maxIoB = max(iob).coerceAtLeast(0.1f)`; fill path color `0x2642A5F5` (blue, 0.15 alpha), line color `0xFF42A5F5`, strokeWidth 1.5f, anti-aliased.
 6. Bolus markers (top 12 px region, `BOLUS_MARKER_HEIGHT=12f`) — only reachable via renderPreview since the complication passes an empty list. Diamond, half-width 2.5f. `bolusColor`: automated+correction → `0xFFE91E63` pink; correction → `0xFFFF5722` orange; mealUnits>0 → `0xFF7C4DFF` purple; else `0xFFFF5722`.
 7. Glucose line + dots: per-segment color from the LEFT reading's `bgColor(...)`; strokeWidth 1f, ROUND cap, anti-aliased. Dots radius 3.5f, per-reading color.

Axes: `minY = min(min(values), low-10).coerceAtLeast(20)`; `maxY = max(max(values), high+10).coerceAtMost(500)`; `yRange = (maxY-minY).coerceAtLeast(1f)`. X: `minX = first.timestampMs`, `maxX = last.timestampMs`, `xRange = (maxX-minX).coerceAtLeast(1f)`. `xPos(t) = graphLeft + ((t-minX)/xRange)*graphWidth`; `yPos(mgDl) = graphBottom - ((mgDl-minY)/yRange)*graphHeight`. Empty reading list returns a blank bitmap early.

`renderPreview()` fabricates 12 readings (120,135,150,145,160,155,140,130,125,110,105,115) at 5-min (300_000 ms) spacing, 4 basal records, 2 bolus records, 4 IoB records, low=70 high=180 urgentLow=55 urgentHigh=250.
edge_cases: The Y clamps 20/500 are documented in docs/contract/safety-constants.md as DISPLAY-ONLY re-expressions of the safety bound, deliberately excluded from the drift guard.
The x-axis spans first→last reading timestamp, not cutoff→now, so a sparse window stretches to fill the width.
When all readings share one timestamp, xRange floors at 1f and every point lands at graphLeft.
The graph complication carries no freshness de-emphasis at all — a 3-hour-old sparkline renders identically to a live one.

capabilities.name: Complication provider: alerts (bell) — the coverage-honesty glance
capabilities.behavior:
`AlertsComplicationDataSource : SuspendingComplicationDataSourceService`. Manifest: SUPPORTED_TYPES `SMALL_IMAGE`, UPDATE_PERIOD_SECONDS **300** — explicitly annotated as 'the complication that must flip to the "not watching / no recent data" cue when the phone stops pushing'. Calls `WatchDataRepository.init(applicationContext)` (added after a bug where it read StateFlows without restoring persisted state).

Icon: `R.drawable.ic_complication_bell` (24dp vector) tinted per render. Tap: `PendingIntent.getActivity(..., requestCode 2001, AlertsActivity, NEW_TASK|CLEAR_TOP, UPDATE_CURRENT|IMMUTABLE)`.

Pure `render(alert, coverage, nowMs): AlertsRender` with colors COLOR_DEFAULT `0xFF9CA3AF` (grey), COLOR_WARNING `0xFFFBBF24` (yellow), COLOR_URGENT `0xFFEF4444` (red). Inputs: `hasActiveAlert = alert != null && !type.equals("none", ignoreCase)`; `isUrgent = type.startsWith("urgent", ignoreCase)`; `alertIsStale = cgmTier(now - alert.timestampMs) == TOO_STALE` (≥15 min); `covered = coverage is Watching`.

Tint (first match wins):
  1. hasActiveAlert && alertIsStale && covered → GREY
  2. hasActiveAlert && alertIsStale (not covered) → YELLOW
  3. isUrgent → RED
  4. hasActiveAlert → YELLOW
  5. !covered → YELLOW
  6. else → GREY
The ordering is load-bearing and documented: 'the stale-alert grey may only render while something is WATCHING: a real alert whose phone then dies ages past the cap and never auto-clears, and quiet grey there would be indistinguishable from the healthy all-clear — suppressing the dead-phone cue in exactly the case it exists for.'

Descriptions: stale alert → `"Alert as of <age> — data stale"` + `", not watching"` when uncovered; urgent → `"Urgent alert active"`; active → `"Alert active (<age>)"`; no alert + NotWatching → `"Monitoring degraded — not watching"`; no alert + NoRecentStatus → `"No recent data from phone"`; no alert + Watching → `"No active alerts"`.
edge_cases: The bell is amber whenever coverage is degraded or unknown, even with zero alerts — the quiet grey bell is reserved for a current 'watching' claim.
Alert age uses the CGM tier (6/15 min), not the pump tier.
Test-pinned: alert age 15min−1ms → yellow + "Alert active (14m ago)"; 15min → grey + "Alert as of 15m ago — data stale" (only when covered).

capabilities.name: Per-buildType WFF provider-package substitution (build-time)
capabilities.behavior:
WFF XML has no build-time variable substitution, and a hardcoded provider package would leave RELEASE faces pointing complications at the DEBUG wear app (dead slots on a fresh production install). `GenerateWatchFaceXmlTask` (a `@CacheableTask` in watchface/build.gradle.kts) reads `src/<flavor>/templates/watchface.xml`, HARD-FAILS with a GradleException if the file contains no `@WEAR_PKG@` token, and writes `raw/watchface.xml` into the variant's generated res with the token replaced by `com.glycemicgpt.mobile.debug` (debug) or `com.glycemicgpt.mobile` (release).

ApplicationIds are set per-variant in `androidComponents.onVariants` to satisfy the Watch Face Push requirement `<client-app-package>.watchfacepush.<identifier>`: base prefix `com.glycemicgpt.mobile[.debug].watchfacepush.glycemicgpt`, plus flavor suffix `""` for digitalFull and `"_mechanical"` for analogMechanical.

Post-build `strip<Variant>WffFiles` task (finalizes assemble), documented in four numbered points: (1) AGP always generates classes.dex even with `hasCode=false` and the DwfValidator REJECTS APKs containing classes.dex; (2) with minSdk ≥ 24 AGP uses only v2/v3 signing but the DwfValidator REQUIRES v1 JAR signing (META-INF/MANIFEST.MF); (3) targetSdk 35 requires v2 minimum; (4) stripping classes.dex invalidates any signature. Steps: `zip -d <apk> classes.dex META-INF/com/android/build/gradle/app-metadata.properties` (exit 0 or 12 accepted, anything else fails); `zipalign -f 4`; `apksigner sign --v1-signing-enabled true --v2-signing-enabled true` using DEBUG_KEYSTORE_FILE env or `~/.android/debug.keystore` with defaults alias `androiddebugkey` / password `android`. Missing keystore → warn and skip (CI only needs the build to succeed). Packaging excludes `/*.properties` and `/*.version` but explicitly NOT META-INF signing files.

`updateAppWatchFaceAssets` rebuilds all four flavor×buildType APKs, verifies each contains a `res/raw/watchface.xml` entry (refusing to commit an asset the drift gate cannot verify), copies them to `app/src/{debug,release}/assets/glycemicgpt-watchface-<flavor>.apk`, and rewrites `watchface/committed-assets.sha256`. A `gradle.taskGraph.whenReady` guard HARD-FAILS the task unless `-Pandroid.enableResourceOptimizations=false` is passed (release builds otherwise shorten `res/raw/watchface.xml` to `res/<xx>.xml`, hiding the entry the drift gate reads).
edge_cases: Release watch face APKs are signed with the DEBUG keystore ('a dedicated release keystore will be added when production distribution is set up. The Watch Face Push API does not enforce Play Store signing').
Release builds set `vcsInfo { include = false }` to keep the release APK byte-structure identical to the hardware-verified debug shape.
Committed asset sizes today: digitalFull debug 33408 B / release 29312 B; analogMechanical debug 17350 B / release 13254 B.

capabilities.name: Watch face push: phone side (WatchFacePusher)
capabilities.behavior:
`@Singleton WatchFacePusher`, runs on `Dispatchers.IO`. `pushWatchFace(variant = DIGITAL_FULL): Result` where `Result = Success(status: String, slotId: String?) | Error(message: String)`.

Sequence:
 1. `hasAsset(variant.assetFilename)` — opens the asset; missing → `Error("Watch face APK not found: <name>")`.
 2. Integrity: looks up `VARIANT_SHA256[variant]` = `BuildConfig.WATCHFACE_DIGITAL_SHA256` / `WATCHFACE_ANALOG_SHA256` (computed by Gradle from the committed per-buildType asset at build time, so the runtime check is always in lockstep). A missing hash mapping throws via `requireNotNull`. `verifyAssetIntegrity` streams the asset through SHA-256 with an 8192-byte buffer and hex-compares; mismatch → `Error("Watch face APK integrity check failed")`.
 3. `findWatchNode()`: `CapabilityClient.getCapability("glycemicgpt_watch_app", FILTER_REACHABLE)`, prefers `isNearby` then any; on exception falls back to `NodeClient.connectedNodes.first()`. Null → `Error("No watch connected")`.
 4. `ChannelClient.openChannel(nodeId, "/glycemicgpt/watchface/push")`, stream the asset to the channel's OutputStream with an 8192-byte buffer.
 5. A watchdog coroutine force-closes the channel after `SEND_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000L` (2 min); the channel is closed exactly once via an `AtomicBoolean.compareAndSet` shared between watchdog and `finally`.
 6. Returns `Success(status = "sent", slotId = null)`. **"sent" means only that the bytes were transferred** — actual install status is logged on the watch side and (today) not relayed back.

Caller: `SettingsViewModel.pushWatchFace()` — guarded by an `AtomicBoolean` (re-entrancy), wraps the call in `withTimeout(PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS = 150_000L)` → `Error("Push timed out")`, sets `WatchFacePushState.Pushing → Success|Error`, and auto-dismisses the result after `AUTO_DISMISS_MS = 5_000L`.
edge_cases: The 150 s ViewModel timeout is deliberately longer than the 120 s pusher watchdog.
No progress reporting during the transfer.
Because the phone never listens for the watch's status message, a validation failure or a denied SET_PUSHED_WATCH_FACE_AS_ACTIVE permission still shows the user 'Watch face sent to watch'.

capabilities.name: Watch face push: watch side receive + install (WatchFaceReceiveService, WatchFaceInstaller, WatchFacePermissionActivity)
capabilities.behavior:
`WatchFaceReceiveService : WearableListenerService`, exported, `foregroundServiceType="dataSync"`, CHANNEL_EVENT filter `pathPrefix="/glycemicgpt/watchface/"`.

`onChannelOpened`: ignores channels whose path != `/glycemicgpt/watchface/push`. Promotes to foreground on the first concurrent push (AtomicInteger + synchronized lock; notification channel `watchface_push` IMPORTANCE_LOW, title "Installing watch face", FOREGROUND_ID 9001, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC`); demotes with `STOP_FOREGROUND_REMOVE` when the count returns to 0. Installs are serialized by a `Mutex`.

`receiveAndInstallWatchFace`:
 1. `WatchFaceInstaller.isSupported()` (API ≥ 36) — else send status `error` / `"Watch Face Push requires Wear OS 6"`, close channel, return (rejected EARLY to avoid a pointless transfer).
 2. Permission gate: if `com.google.wear.permission.SET_PUSHED_WATCH_FACE_AS_ACTIVE` is not granted, start the transparent `WatchFacePermissionActivity` (`FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`), `delay(3000)`, re-check; still denied → status `error` / `"Permission denied -- cannot activate watch face"`, close, return.
 3. `File.createTempFile("watchface-push-", ".apk", cacheDir)`; read the channel InputStream with `copyWithLimit(..., MAX_APK_SIZE_BYTES = 50 MB)` (8192-byte buffer, `currentCoroutineContext().ensureActive()` between chunks for cooperative cancellation at ~8 KB boundaries; exceeding the limit throws IllegalStateException). A watchdog coroutine force-closes the channel after `RECEIVE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000L` — closing the channel closes the socket, which is the only way to unblock a stalled blocking `InputStream.read()`.
 4. Empty file → status `error` / `"Empty APK received"`.
 5. Magic-byte check: first 4 bytes must equal `0x50 0x4B 0x03 0x04` (PK zip header) → else `"Invalid APK format"`.
 6. Install under `withContext(NonCancellable)` using `applicationContext` (the service scope may be cancelled by onDestroy after the channel event but before install completes).
 7. `finally`: delete temp file and close the channel (both NonCancellable).

Status messages: `sendStatus(status, slotId?, error?)` builds a `key=value` newline payload (`status=`, `slot=`, `error=`) and broadcasts it to ALL `NodeClient.connectedNodes` on `/glycemicgpt/watchface/status`. `sanitize()` replaces `\n`, `\r` with space and `=` with `_` to prevent delimiter injection. Statuses used: `installed`, `updated`, `error`.

`WatchFaceInstaller(context)` — `Result = Installed(slotId) | Updated(slotId) | Error(message)`; `isSupported()` = `Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 36`. All four public methods (`installOrUpdate`, `listFaces`, `isActive`, `remove`) short-circuit on unsupported devices (Error / emptyList / false / false) and delegate to `@RequiresApi(36)` privates so the WatchFacePushManager class never loads on older API levels.

`installOrUpdateInternal`:
 - `findExistingFace()` = first installed face whose `packageName.contains(".watchfacepush.")` (WATCHFACE_PACKAGE_MARKER — matches both debug `com.glycemicgpt.mobile.debug.watchfacepush.glycemicgpt` and release).
 - APK must exist and be readable.
 - `generateValidationToken(apkFile)` on `Dispatchers.IO`: `DwfValidatorFactory.create().validate(apkFile, context.packageName)` — uses the ACTUAL package name including `.debug`, because the Push API requires the watch face package to start with the client's actual package name and both validator and API must see the same string. Non-empty `failures()` → each logged, returns null → `Error("Watch face APK failed validation")`. Null/empty token despite no failures also returns null.
 - Existing → `updateWatchFace(slotId, pfd, token)`; else `addWatchFace(pfd, token)`. ParcelFileDescriptor opened MODE_READ_ONLY and closed in a `finally` each time.
 - SLOT-LIMIT RETRY: on `AddWatchFaceException` whose `message?.contains("limit", ignoreCase = true)`, calls `removeAllOurFaces()` (removes every installed face matching the marker) and retries `addWatchFace` ONCE. Documented as fragile: 'AddWatchFaceException does not expose error codes or subtypes, so we rely on message text matching. This is the only detection method available in the current Wear OS Push API.'
 - `setWatchFaceAsActive(slotId)`; a `SetWatchFaceAsActiveException` is caught and only warned ('user may need to set manually').
 - SAMSUNG WEAR OS 6 WORKAROUND (fresh installs only, `existing == null`): `rebindComplications()` waits `delay(1000)` then re-runs `updateWatchFace(slotId, pfd, token)` with the SAME APK. Rationale: `addWatchFace()` evaluates the WFF `DefaultProviderPolicy` and creates complication bindings, but they are immediately deactivated because the face isn't active yet; `setWatchFaceAsActive()` doesn't re-trigger the policy. The re-update re-evaluates the policy while the face IS active so the bindings persist. Failures are only warned.
 - `rethrowIfCancellation(e)` walks the cause chain and rethrows any nested `CancellationException` before converting to an Error result.
edge_cases: The 3-second permission wait is a fixed sleep, not a result callback — a user who takes longer than 3 s to tap Allow gets 'Permission denied'.
`WatchFacePermissionActivity` finishes immediately if the permission is already granted; otherwise launches `ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission` and finishes on the callback.

The validator's transitive EPL-1.0 XPath-2.0 processor (`com.rackspace.eclipse.webtools.sourceediting:org.eclipse.wst.xml.xpath2.processor`) is EXCLUDED from the dependency because EPL-1.0 is incompatible with the app's GPL-3.0 for a combined distributed work. `WatchFaceValidatorTest` (instrumented) proves the validator still returns a non-empty token without it — 'If a future validator version genuinely needs it to parse the WFF, that test fails — do not re-add the dependency without a license decision.'
Concurrent pushes are serialized by the mutex but the foreground counter is separate, so a second push arriving during an install keeps the notification alive.

capabilities.name: Watch APK self-update over Data Layer (WearApkPusher → WatchApkReceiveService → UpdateInstallReceiver)
capabilities.behavior:
Phone: `SettingsViewModel.checkForWatchUpdate()` (guarded by `WATCH_UPDATE_CHECK_COOLDOWN_MS = 10_000L` and a Checking-state guard) reads `/glycemicgpt/watch/version` for `watch_update_ch` (default "stable") and `watch_dev_build` (default 0), then `WearAppUpdateChecker.check(versionCode, channel, devBuild)`.

`WearAppUpdateChecker` (OkHttp, connectTimeout 15 s, readTimeout 120 s): stable → `https://api.github.com/repos/lumose-health/android-unofficial/releases/latest` with asset suffix `-release.apk`; dev → `.../releases/tags/dev-latest` with suffix `-debug.apk`. Asset must start with prefix `GlycemicGPT-Wear-`. Dev channel compares `parseDevRunNumber(assetName) > watchDevBuildNumber`; stable compares `parseVersionCode(tag minus "v") > watchVersionCode`. HTTP 403 → "Rate limit exceeded. Try again later."; 404 on dev → "No dev release available yet.".

`downloadWearApk(url, fileName, expectedSize)`: enforces `isHttpsUrl` ('an APK download is a code-execution path: enforce https in code rather than relying solely on the network_security_config pin') and `isAllowedDownloadHost`, sanitizes the filename, deletes all previously cached APKs, streams into `cacheDir/wear_apk_updates/` with an 8192 buffer, aborts over `MAX_DOWNLOAD_SIZE_BYTES = 100 MB`, and verifies `apkFile.length() == expectedSize` when expectedSize > 0 (mismatch → delete + error).

`WearApkPusher` mirrors WatchFacePusher but streams a local `File`, uses channel `/glycemicgpt/watch/apk/push`, and `SEND_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000L` (5 min, 'wear APKs are larger than WFF watch faces'). Rejects a missing/zero-length file. Same CapabilityClient→NodeClient discovery, same AtomicBoolean close-once + watchdog. Result `Success("sent") | Error(msg)`.

Watch: `WatchApkReceiveService : WearableListenerService`, exported, dataSync foreground (channel `watch_apk_update`, "Updating watch app", FOREGROUND_ID 9002), CHANNEL_EVENT filter `pathPrefix="/glycemicgpt/watch/apk/"`. `MAX_APK_SIZE_BYTES = 100 MB`, `RECEIVE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000L`, same PK magic-byte check, same mutex + watchdog + NonCancellable pattern. Additionally requires `packageManager.canRequestPackageInstalls()` → else status `error` / "Install permission not granted on watch". Sends status `installing` before committing.

`installApk`: `PackageInstaller.SessionParams(MODE_FULL_INSTALL)` with `setAppPackageName(packageName)`; `openWrite("watch_apk_update", 0, apkFile.length())`, copy, `session.fsync(out)`; commit with a `PendingIntent.getBroadcast(..., sessionId, UpdateInstallReceiver with ACTION_INSTALL_RESULT + extra session_id, FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT|FLAG_MUTABLE)`. Any exception → `session.abandon()` then rethrow.

`UpdateInstallReceiver`: on `STATUS_PENDING_USER_ACTION` extracts `Intent.EXTRA_INTENT` (API-33-aware getParcelableExtra) and starts it with FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK. On `STATUS_SUCCESS` just logs (the process is normally already killed and restarted). Otherwise uses `goAsync()` and best-effort sends `status=error\nerror=Install failed: status=<n> <msg>` to all connected nodes on `/glycemicgpt/watch/apk/status`.

Phone UI state machine (`WatchAppUpdateState`): `Idle → Checking → (Available|UpToDate|Error)`; `Available → Downloading → Pushing → Installing → Success`. Because no status message is consumed, `Installing → Success` is driven purely by a 15-second timer (`delay(15_000L)` then flip if still Installing). Re-entrancy guarded by `watchUpdateInProgress: AtomicBoolean`; the downloaded APK is deleted in a `finally`.
edge_cases: The APK bytes are NOT signature- or hash-verified on the watch beyond the PK magic bytes; `setAppPackageName` plus Android's own signature check on replace is the guard.
'Success' is a timer, not a confirmation — a failed install that fires the receiver still shows Success if the error message arrives with no listener.
`docs/mobile/wear-os.md` documents the manual ADB path as the supported install route today; the push path is described as the Wear OS 6+ convenience.

capabilities.name: Phone→watch monitoring-status mirror + watch-local decay (GLY-116 axis a)
capabilities.behavior:
`WearMonitoringStatusForwarder.start(scope)` runs on the pump service's `serviceScope` (started in `PumpConnectionService` right after the in-app coverage collectors). Pipeline: `appSettingsStore.debugFastStalenessFlow().flatMapLatest { fast -> timeoutMs = FreshnessPolicy.cgm(fast).staleAfterMs; combine(alertFloorStatusProvider.observe(), tickerFlow(heartbeatPeriodMs(timeoutMs))) { status, _ -> status to timeoutMs } }`, with `.retryWhen { _, _ -> delay(RETRY_DELAY_MS = 5_000L); true }` so a failed coverage stream always resubscribes ('a coverage-status stream must never die silently').

`heartbeatPeriodMs(timeoutMs) = (timeoutMs / 2).coerceAtLeast(MIN_HEARTBEAT_MS = 5_000L)` — 'half the advertised timeout, so a single dropped DataItem does not decay the wrist to "no recent data" while the phone is actually alive and watching'. Production: `FreshnessPolicy.CGM.staleAfterMs = 360_000 ms` (6 min) → heartbeat every 180_000 ms (3 min). Debug fast-staleness: `CGM_DEBUG_FAST.staleAfterMs = 20_000 ms` → heartbeat floored at 5_000 ms.

Re-sending on a heartbeat (not only on change) is load-bearing: the provider stream deduplicates, so a healthy steady state would emit exactly once and a watch that then lost the phone (process death, Bluetooth drop) would hold a frozen 'watching' forever. Each heartbeat restarts the watch's local timeout; SILENCE longer than the advertised window is the watch's signal that the phone is gone.

Wire encoding (`AlertFloorStatus.toWire()`): `ServerActive → ("server_active", null)`, `FloorWatching → ("floor_watching", null)`, `FloorNotWatching(reason) → ("not_watching", reason.name)`. Reasons are the phone enum NAMES verbatim: `NOTIFICATIONS_DENIED`, `THRESHOLDS_NOT_SYNCED`, `THRESHOLDS_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `PUMP_DISCONNECTED`, `NO_FRESH_READING` — pinned by contract constants so a rename breaks the contract test instead of silently sending a string the watch renders as generic copy.

Upstream `alertFloorStatus(...)` decision order on the phone: not degraded (network REACHABLE && SSE CONNECTED) → ServerActive; else !canNotify → NOTIFICATIONS_DENIED; else !thresholdsConfigured → THRESHOLDS_NOT_SYNCED (backend configured) or THRESHOLDS_NOT_CONFIGURED; else !pumpConnected → PUMP_DISCONNECTED; else fresh reading → FloorWatching; else NO_FRESH_READING.

The watch performs NO coverage decision of its own — it renders this status and locally decays it (see `WatchDataRepository.coverageFrom`).
edge_cases: The forwarder only runs while `PumpConnectionService` is alive — with no pump service running the watch receives no heartbeat and correctly decays to 'no recent data'.
The watch clamps the advertised timeout to 10 s..30 min regardless of what the phone sends.

capabilities.name: Watch freshness policy (WatchFreshness) — mirrored, not shared
capabilities.behavior:
A deliberate mirror of the phone's `FreshnessPolicy.CGM`/`PUMP` because 'the wear module deliberately has no dependency on the phone app… a drift would make the watch call the same reading fresher or staler than the phone does.'

Constants: `CGM_STALE_AFTER_MS = 6 * 60_000` (360 000), `CGM_TOO_STALE_AFTER_MS = 15 * 60_000` (900 000), `PUMP_STALE_AFTER_MS = 15 * 60_000` (900 000), `PUMP_TOO_STALE_AFTER_MS = 60 * 60_000` (3 600 000), `DEFAULT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS = CGM_STALE_AFTER_MS` (fallback when a pre-GLY-116 phone omits the timeout key), `STATUS_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS = 60_000` (mirrors the phone's `ALERT_FLOOR_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS`).

`classify(ageMs, staleAfterMs, tooStaleAfterMs): Tier` — half-open boundaries matching the phone: `ageMs < -60_000 → TOO_STALE`; `ageMs < staleAfterMs → FRESH`; `ageMs < tooStaleAfterMs → STALE`; else `TOO_STALE`. Convenience wrappers `cgmTier(ageMs)` and `pumpTier(ageMs)`.

Documented rationale for the skew handling: small negative ages are ROUTINE (surfaces sample 'now' on their own cadence; pump clocks drift by seconds) and failing them closed would flap healthy feeds; a LARGE negative age means the watch clock jumped BACKWARD, which understates every age — so both honesty axes fail closed on it (coverage → NoRecentStatus, feed tiers → TOO_STALE).

Axis (b) statement: 'every wrist surface that shows a pushed value (BG, IoB, the last alert) ages it against the WATCH's own clock with these tiers, independently of the mirrored "watching" status — a dead phone freezes pushes, and only local aging turns that frozen snapshot into an honest "no recent data".'
edge_cases: Boundary pairs pinned: CGM 6min−1 FRESH / 6min STALE; CGM 15min−1 STALE / 15min TOO_STALE; PUMP 15min−1 FRESH / 15min STALE; PUMP 60min−1 STALE / 60min TOO_STALE; age −60_000 FRESH / −60_001 TOO_STALE.

capabilities.name: Glucose validation, unit conversion and color banding (GlucoseDisplayUtils, GlucoseUnit)
capabilities.behavior:
`MGDL_PER_MMOL: Double = 18.0156` — 'the exact glucose mass-to-molarity factor and the single canonical constant. Pinned to match the phone `GlucoseFormat.MGDL_PER_MMOL` (and the backend `MGDL_PER_MMOL`) exactly… Never introduce a second value (18.02 / 18.0182).' Guarded by `SafetyConstantWearGuardTest` and documented in docs/contract/safety-constants.md.

`isValidGlucose(mgDl) = mgDl in 20..500` — the platform-wide invariant.

`sanitizeThresholds(rawLow, rawHigh, rawUrgentLow, rawUrgentHigh)` in strict order, each clamp depending on the previous:
  `low = rawLow.coerceIn(40, 200)`
  `high = rawHigh.coerceIn(maxOf(low + 1, 100), 400)`
  `urgentLow = rawUrgentLow.coerceIn(20, low)`
  `urgentHigh = rawUrgentHigh.coerceIn(high, 500)`
This guarantees `20 ≤ urgentLow ≤ low < high ≤ urgentHigh ≤ 500` for any input.

`bgColor(mgDl, low, high, urgentLow, urgentHigh)` — takes NO unit (the display preference cannot reach it): `mgDl <= urgentLow || mgDl >= urgentHigh → 0xFFEF4444` (red); `mgDl <= low || mgDl >= high → 0xFFEAB308` (yellow); else `0xFF22C55E` (green). Boundaries are INCLUSIVE on the warning side.

`alertColor(type)`: `urgent_low`/`urgent_high` → red `0xFFEF4444`; `low`/`high` → yellow `0xFFEAB308`; else `Color.WHITE`.

`formatGlucose(mgDl, unit)`: MGDL → `mgDl.toString()`; MMOL → `String.format(Locale.US, "%.1f", mgDl / 18.0156)` — 'divide once, round LAST'; `Locale.US` keeps a dot decimal separator matching the phone even under a comma-decimal locale. `unitLabel`: "mg/dL" / "mmol/L". `formatWithLabel` = `"<number> <label>"`.
DOC WARNING: 'Display-only: never feed the result back into isValidGlucose, bgColor, sanitizeThresholds, or any plotting geometry — those all stay mg/dL.'
Cross-surface fixture pinned by test (phone, web, API must agree): 54→"3.0", 70→"3.9", 99→"5.5", 100→"5.6", 120→"6.7", 180→"10.0", 250→"13.9", 400→"22.2".

`formatAge(ageMs)`: `< -60_000` → `"unknown time"` (watch clock jumped backward — saying so avoids the incoherent 'as of just now — data stale'); `< 0` → `"just now"`; `minutes < 1` → `"just now"`; `< 60` → `"<m>m ago"`; else `"<h>h <m>m ago"`.

`GlucoseUnit` enum: `MGDL("mgdl")`, `MMOL("mmol")`; `fromWire(value: String?)` is case-insensitive and NEVER throws — unknown/null falls back to MGDL. Deliberately duplicated from the phone's enum because the modules cannot share code.
edge_cases: A value of exactly `low` or exactly `high` bands as WARNING (yellow), not green.
65 mg/dL displays as "65" or "3.6" but bands yellow in both — the band reads the raw mg/dL, never the formatted string.
`formatAge` differs from the phone's `relativeAgeLabel`, which uses seconds and adds a days tier.

capabilities.name: On-watch alerts screen (AlertsActivity)
capabilities.behavior:
`ComponentActivity` + Wear Compose (`MaterialTheme`, `Scaffold(timeText = { TimeText() })`), exported=false, launched only by the Alerts complication tap. Collects `alert`, `glucoseUnit` and `monitoringStatus` StateFlows and re-evaluates on a `NOW_TICK_MS = 15_000L` ticker ('both honesty axes decay with time, not only with new pushes… a shown alert must grey out and a "watching" claim must expire even when nothing new arrives — that silence is exactly the signal').

WITH an alert:
 - `alertAgeMs = nowMs - alert.timestampMs`; `isDataStale = cgmTier(alertAgeMs) == TOO_STALE` (≥15 min); `isUrgent = type.startsWith("urgent", ignoreCase)`.
 - Color: stale → COLOR_MUTED `0xFF9CA3AF`; urgent → COLOR_URGENT `0xFFEF4444`; else COLOR_WARNING `0xFFFBBF24`.
 - Title = `formatAlertType(type)` (underscores → spaces, each word title-cased) in `typography.title3`.
 - BG value shown ONLY when `alert.bgValue in 20..500` (the gate compares the RAW mg/dL Int; only the rendered text converts), at 20.sp via `formatWithLabel(bgValue, unit)`.
 - Age line always visible (testTag `alert_age`): `"as of <age> — data stale"` when stale, else `formatAge(age)`. Documented: 'the alert may still be true, nobody can currently vouch either way, and a silent retraction to "All clear" would be the opposite lie.'
 - Message text when non-blank, `maxLines = 3`.
 - When `isDataStale && coverage !is Watching`, an extra amber line `"Not watching — check your phone"` (testTag `stale_alert_not_watching`) — 'without this line, a dead phone behind a stale alert would surface no "not watching" cue on this screen at all.'
 - Dismiss button (background `0xFF374151`, 80% width): guarded by a `dismissing` flag; on click sends `WearMessageSender.sendAlertDismiss(context)`, calls `WatchDataRepository.clearAlert()` locally, and finishes. Label flips to "Dismissing..." and the button is disabled.

WITHOUT an alert (`NoAlertContent(coverage)`) — three mutually exclusive renders:
 - `Watching`: title "No Active Alert" + green `0xFF4ADE80` "All clear" (testTag `all_clear`). This is the ONLY quiet reassurance path.
 - `NotWatching(reason)`: amber title "Not watching" (testTag `not_watching`) + `notWatchingReasonCopy(reason)` + muted caption "Caregiver & AI alerts are paused — they need the backend."
 - `NoRecentStatus`: muted title "No recent data" (testTag `no_recent_status`) + "The watch hasn't heard from your phone recently. Alerts may not arrive."

`notWatchingReasonCopy` (internal, not private, so `AlertsCopyTest` can pin every arm — 'a dropped or renamed arm silently degrades to the generic copy, the wear analogue of the store's silent-disarm'):
  NOTIFICATIONS_DENIED → "Monitoring degraded — allow notifications on your phone."
  THRESHOLDS_NOT_SYNCED → "Monitoring degraded — alert thresholds haven't synced yet."
  THRESHOLDS_NOT_CONFIGURED → "Alerts off — set alert thresholds in the phone's Settings."
  PUMP_DISCONNECTED → "Monitoring degraded — pump is disconnected."
  NO_FRESH_READING → "Monitoring degraded — no fresh glucose readings."
  null/unknown → "Monitoring degraded — nothing is watching for lows or highs."
edge_cases: The dismiss optimistically clears the local alert even if `sendAlertDismiss` returns false (phone unreachable) — the phone's copy then stays and will re-push on the next alert refresh.
An alert with bgValue outside 20..500 (or the sanitized 0) shows the type + age but no number.

capabilities.name: On-watch AI chat (ChatActivity) + phone relay (WearChatRelayService)
capabilities.behavior:
WATCH SIDE — `ChatActivity : ComponentActivity`, exported=false, launched from the Chat complication tap or with `EXTRA_QUERY = "chat_query"` (truncated to `MAX_QUERY_LENGTH = 500`). `onCreate` calls `WatchDataRepository.clearChat()` first.

TTS: initialized only if `watchFaceConfig.aiTtsEnabled`. `TextToSpeech(applicationContext)`; on SUCCESS sets `Locale.getDefault()`, marks ready, then `applyConfiguredVoice()` — matches `aiTtsVoice` against `engine.voices` by name, falls back to the default locale voice with a warning when unavailable. `speakIfEnabled(text)` strips Markdown, skips blanks, and speaks with `QUEUE_FLUSH` and a random `UUID` utterance id. On response Success the spoken text is `state.response + ". This is not medical advice."`, guarded against re-speaking the same response via `spokenResponseId`. `onDestroy` stops and shuts down the engine.

Markdown stripping (pre-compiled regexes): bold `\*\*(.+?)\*\*`→$1, italic `\*(.+?)\*`→$1, heading `^#{1,6}\s+` (MULTILINE)→"", bullet `^[-*]\s+` (MULTILINE)→"- ", numbered `^\d+\.\s+` (MULTILINE)→"", link `\[(.+?)]\(.+?\)`→$1, inline code `` `(.+?)` ``→$1, then trim.

UI states (`ChatState` sealed: `Idle | Loading | Success(response, disclaimer) | Error(message)`):
 - Idle with a prefill query → shows the query text + a "Send" button.
 - Idle without prefill → title "Ask AI", a blue (`0xFF3B82F6`) voice button labelled "Ask a question..." launching `RecognizerIntent.ACTION_RECOGNIZE_SPEECH` with `LANGUAGE_MODEL_FREE_FORM` and prompt "Ask a question..."; `ActivityNotFoundException` → "Voice input not available"; empty/blank recognition result → "Couldn't understand. Try again."; then three QUICK_QUERIES buttons: **"How am I doing?", "Breakfast advice", "Why is my BG high?"**.
 - Loading → `CircularProgressIndicator` + "Asking AI...".
 - Success → markdown-stripped response (caption1) + `state.disclaimer.ifBlank { "Not medical advice. Consult your doctor." }` in grey `0xFF9CA3AF` caption3.
 - Error → red "Error" title + message, `maxLines = 4`.

Watch-side timeout: a `LaunchedEffect(chatState)` waits `CHAT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000L` while Loading and, if still Loading, sets `Error("Request timed out. Check phone connection.")`. `DisposableEffect` clears chat state on dispose only if still Loading.

`sendQuery`: trims and truncates to 500, blank → `Error("Please enter a question")`; sets Loading; `WearMessageSender.sendChatRequest` false → `Error("Phone not connected")`; exception → `Error("Failed to send request")`.

PHONE SIDE — `WearChatRelayService : WearableListenerService` (`@AndroidEntryPoint`), exported, `foregroundServiceType="dataSync"`. Handles CHAT_REQUEST_PATH and ALERT_DISMISS_PATH.

`handleChatRequest`: decodes UTF-8 and trims. Empty → `sendError("Empty message")`. `length > MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 500` → `sendError("Message too long (max 500 chars)")`. **BLE-only mode gate (GLY-146)**: if `!authTokenStore.isBackendConfigured()` → `sendError(NO_BACKEND_MESSAGE = "AI chat needs a GlycemicGPT server — none is set up on your phone.")`. Documented: 'honest terminal copy… names the permanent condition and where to fix it, and deliberately never says "try again" — retrying cannot help until a server is set up.' Checked BEFORE the foreground promotion.
Then `startWork()` promotes to foreground (channel `watch_chat_relay`, IMPORTANCE_LOW, "Processing watch request"/"Asking AI...", ongoing+silent, NOTIFICATION_ID 3, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_TYPE_DATA_SYNC` on API ≥ 34) and `runBlocking { withTimeoutOrNull(CHAT_API_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000L) { chatRepository.sendMessage(text) } }`. Documented rationale: 'Promote to foreground so Android doesn't kill the process during the long-running LLM API call (20-60s). Then block the binder thread so GMS doesn't unbind the WearableListenerService before the response arrives. onMessageReceived runs on a background binder thread (not main), so blocking won't cause ANR.'
Timeout (null) → `sendError("Request timed out. Try again later.")`. Success → JSON `{"response":..., "disclaimer":...}` on CHAT_RESPONSE_PATH. Failure → `sanitizeErrorMessage(error)` mapping (case-insensitive substring): contains "timeout" → "Request timed out. Try again later."; "Unable to resolve host" → "No internet connection."; "401" → "Session expired. Open phone app to sign in."; "500" → "Server error. Try again later."; else "Something went wrong. Try again later."

Foreground lifecycle uses `activeWorkCount: AtomicInteger` so concurrent work items (chat + dismiss) keep the foreground state until ALL complete; `finishWork` clamps to 0 and calls `stopForeground(STOP_FOREGROUND_REMOVE)`.

`WearMessageSender` (watch, `object`): `WEARABLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000L` wraps EVERY await. `getPhoneNodeId` uses `CapabilityClient.getCapability("glycemicgpt_chat_relay", FILTER_REACHABLE)` preferring `isNearby`, then any capability node, then `NodeClient.connectedNodes.first()`; any exception → null.
edge_cases: The watch's 30 s timeout is much shorter than the phone's 90 s API timeout: a slow LLM response arriving at 45 s will overwrite the displayed 'Request timed out' error with a Success state if the screen is still open.
The disclaimer is the backend's when present; the watch supplies its own default only when the field is blank.
The Chat complication does not check whether a backend is configured — the error only surfaces after a round trip.
Quick queries are hardcoded on the watch, not configurable from the phone.

capabilities.name: Alert dismiss flow (watch → phone)
capabilities.behavior:
Watch: `WearMessageSender.sendAlertDismiss(context)` sends an **EMPTY `ByteArray(0)`** on `/glycemicgpt/alert/dismiss` (10 s timeout), then the UI clears the local alert and finishes.

Phone `WearChatRelayService.handleAlertDismiss()`: `startWork()` (foreground), `runBlocking { alertRepository.getLatestUnacknowledgedServerId() }`; if non-null, `alertRepository.acknowledgeAlert(serverId)`. Documented: 'acknowledgeAlert marks the row locally BEFORE the server POST, so the watch's clearAlert below is truthful even when the backend is unreachable — the alert can't re-fire; the server sync is deferred to the reconcile.' Either way it then calls `wearDataSender.clearAlert()`, which pushes `alert_type="none"` back to the watch; `GlycemicDataListenerService` sets `WatchDataRepository.alert = null` and always fires an Alerts complication update.

**KNOWN LIMITATION, documented in docs/dev/wear-os-architecture.md:112**: 'Alert dismiss sends an empty payload — the phone acknowledges the latest unacknowledged alert by timestamp. If multiple alerts arrive in quick succession, the wrong alert could be dismissed. A future improvement should include the alert ID in the dismiss payload for exact matching.'
edge_cases: Dismiss does NOT clear the phone's `previousAlertType` latch in PumpPollingOrchestrator, so an ongoing alert episode will re-push (and re-buzz on the 30-min re-alarm cadence) after a wrist dismiss.

capabilities.name: Phone→watch alert relay state machine (PumpPollingOrchestrator)
capabilities.behavior:
Runs inside `processCgmReading(reading, nowMs)`. Alert types are mapped from the server vocabulary via `SERVER_TO_WATCH_ALERT_TYPE`: `LOW_URGENT→"urgent_low"`, `LOW_WARNING→"low"`, `HIGH_WARNING→"high"`, `HIGH_URGENT→"urgent_high"`. A missing mapping logs a warning and yields null — 'a mapping gap may cost the watch relay, never the alert-floor hand-off.'

**GLY-116 AC-A data-trust gate**: the whole relay alert block is skipped unless `alertFloor.isReadingAlertable(reading, nowMs)` — the same bound the on-device alert floor fires from (`!isWallClockRewound(nowMs)` && `alertThresholdStore.isConfigured()` && the reading is strictly FRESH under `FreshnessPolicy.cgm(debugFastStaleness)` with the −60 s future-skew guard). Documented: 'A not-alertable reading skips the WHOLE relay alert block: no sendAlert, no clearAlert, latch untouched. Retracting the shown alert here would flip a possibly-still-true low into the watch's reassuring "All clear" off data nobody can vouch for; the watch ages the shown alert out on its own clock instead (axis b).'

The block is serialized under `watchRelayMutex` (reachable concurrently from the poll loop, Home manual refresh, and the debug inject) — 'the previousAlertType read-check-write must be atomic or an overlap can double-send or drop a needed clearAlert.'

Transitions:
 - NEW crossing (`watchAlertType != null && != previousAlertType`): `sendAlert(rebuzz = true)`; set `previousAlertType`, `lastAlertSentAtMs = lastAlertBuzzAtMs = nowMs`.
 - ONGOING same type: `rebuzz = nowMs - lastAlertBuzzAtMs >= WRIST_ALERT_REBUZZ_MS`; send when `rebuzz || nowMs - lastAlertSentAtMs >= WRIST_ALERT_REFRESH_MS`. `WRIST_ALERT_REFRESH_MS = 5 * 60_000L` (5 min) — 'silent refreshes that keep the wrist copy's timestamp current, so axis (b) never greys a still-live alert as "data stale" (the CGM STALE band starts at 6 min; 5-min refreshes keep the shown alert inside it)'. `WRIST_ALERT_REBUZZ_MS = AlertFloor.FLOOR_COOLDOWN_MS = 30 * 60_000L` (30 min) — 'with the floor notification local-only (D4), the relay owns the wrist's re-alarm — the wrist must never go permanently silent on an ongoing emergency while the phone keeps alarming.'
 - RECOVERY: only when `serverAlertType == null && previousAlertType != null` → `clearAlert()`, `previousAlertType = null`. Keyed on the CLASSIFICATION being in-range, not on `watchAlertType == null`, because a mapping gap also yields null and clearing there would retract a possibly-still-true alert.

Alert message text: `"<alertLabel(type)> <GlucoseFormat.formatWithLabel(mgDl, unit)>"` where alertLabel maps `urgent_low`→"URGENT LOW", `urgent_high`→"URGENT HIGH", `low`→"LOW", `high`→"HIGH", else "".

Documented wrist-alert path inventory after GLY-116: this relay (gated on `isReadingAlertable`) and the bridged SERVER notification (different glucose source, must stay bridged); the local alert-floor notification is deliberately local-only 'so a single fresh low is one wrist experience, not three.'
edge_cases: `clearAlert()` sends `rebuzz = true` (the default) — harmless because the watch only vibrates for non-"none" types.
When the reading is not alertable and an alert is already shown, the wrist copy simply ages out on the watch clock (grey at 15 min) rather than being retracted.

capabilities.name: Compact history overlay wire format (WearHistorySerializer)
capabilities.behavior:
Two mirrored objects (`encode*` on the phone, `decode*` on the watch), little-endian `ByteBuffer`, fixed-size records:
 - BASAL_RECORD_SIZE = **13** bytes: `rate` Float(4) + `timestampMs` Long(8) + `flags` byte(1). Flags: bit 0 = isAutomated, bits 1–2 = activityMode (0=NONE, 1=SLEEP, 2=EXERCISE), decoded as `(flags shr 1) and 0x03`.
 - BOLUS_RECORD_SIZE = **21** bytes: `units` Float(4) + `correctionUnits` Float(4) + `mealUnits` Float(4) + `timestampMs` Long(8) + `flags` byte(1). Flags: bit 0 = isAutomated, bit 1 (value 2) = isCorrection.
 - IOB_RECORD_SIZE = **12** bytes: `iob` Float(4) + `timestampMs` Long(8).

Watch-side `hasEnoughBytes(data, count, recordSize)` guards every decode: rejects `count < 0` and computes `count.toLong() * recordSize.toLong() <= data.size.toLong()` **using Long arithmetic to prevent Int overflow**; an undersized buffer returns `emptyList()` rather than throwing.

Phone sender caps each type at `MAX_HISTORY_RECORDS = 500` via `takeLast(500)` over the last 6 hours (`Instant.now().minus(6, ChronoUnit.HOURS)`), with the documented sizing: '500 basal × 13B = 6.5KB, 500 bolus × 21B = 10.5KB, 500 IoB × 12B = 6KB' — 'to stay well under the 100KB DataItem limit'. Sent from the SLOW poll loop (every 300 s). `activityModeToInt` is an explicit `when` mapping 'to avoid ordinal-dependence on PumpActivityMode enum order'.
edge_cases: The wire format carries no bolus category field even though `BolusHistoryRecord` has a `category` property (always "").
The listener applies a second count gate (`count <= 500`) on top of the serializer's byte-length check.

capabilities.name: Full-screen interactive graph on the watch (GraphDetailActivity)
capabilities.behavior:
Compose `Canvas` graph launched by the Graph complication tap. Shows "Not enough data" when `cgmHistory.size < MIN_READINGS (3)`.

Layout constants: `GRAPH_PADDING = 28f` (left, for Y labels), `GRAPH_PADDING_RIGHT = 8f`, `GRAPH_PADDING_TOP = 8f`, `GRAPH_PADDING_BOTTOM = 20f` (time labels). Y clamps: `Y_MIN_DEFAULT = 40`, `Y_MAX_DEFAULT = 400` (note: DIFFERENT from the sparkline's 20/500). `minY = min(min(values), low-10).coerceAtLeast(40)`, `maxY = max(max(values), high+10).coerceAtMost(400)`.

Uses ALL available history (not just the range window) 'so there is data to pan into'. Pan: `detectDragGestures` accumulates `panOffsetPx += dragAmount.x` (positive = drag right = scroll back in time), clamped to `0f .. maxPanPx` where `maxPanPx = (scrollableMs / rangeMs) * graphWidth` and `scrollableMs = now - dataStartMs - rangeMs` (0 when non-positive). `computeViewport` converts pan px to ms, sets `viewportEnd = (now - panMs).coerceIn(min(dataStartMs+rangeMs, now), now)` and `viewportStart = viewportEnd - rangeMs`.

Tap: `findNearestReading` recomputes the same geometry, picks the minimum squared distance, and returns null when `nearestDist > TAP_RADIUS_SQ = 2500f` (50 px radius). Tooltip text is `"<formatWithLabel(mgDl, unit)>  <h:mm a>"`, drawn as a `0xCC000000` rounded rect (corner radius 8f, height 30f, horizontal padding 10f) clamped to canvas bounds, positioned `tooltip.y - 30 - 14` above the dot.

Draw order (10 layers): mode bands → target range band → threshold lines WITH numeric Y-axis labels (right-aligned, `GraphPaints.thresholdLabel` white 0.7 alpha, textSize 20f, fake-bold; the printed number converts to the unit but `yPos` stays mg/dL) → basal stepped area (`BASAL_AREA_HEIGHT = 24f`, fill alpha 0.15, top stroke alpha 0.6, step line alpha 0.4 when |Δy| > 0.5f) → IoB area (`IOB_AREA_HEIGHT = 28f`, stroke width 1.5f) → bolus markers (diamond half 4f, top offset 4f, with a unit label above: integral units render `"3u"`, else `"%.1fu"`, plus a category label; automated+correction with no category label → `"<units> Auto"`; x clamped to `graphRect.left+16 .. graphRect.right-16`) → glucose line (`GLUCOSE_LINE_WIDTH = 2f`, segments outside the visible x-range skipped) → glucose dots (`GLUCOSE_DOT_RADIUS = 5f`, off-screen dots skipped) → time axis → tooltip.

Time axis interval by viewport range: ≤1h → 900_000 ms (15-min marks); ≤3h → 3_600_000 ms (1-hour); else 7_200_000 ms (2-hour). Ticks are aligned to clean LOCAL-time minute boundaries via `Calendar` (seconds/millis zeroed, minute rounded up to the next interval multiple) 'so tick marks align to clean minute boundaries regardless of UTC offset'. Labels use `SimpleDateFormat("h:mm", Locale.getDefault())`; tooltips use `"h:mm a"`. All `android.graphics.Paint` and `SimpleDateFormat` instances are pre-allocated in lazily-initialized objects to avoid allocating inside `DrawScope` / the draw loop.

Footer label: `"<H>h  |  <N> readings"` in grey `0xFF9CA3AF`.

This is the ONLY surface that honors `config.showBolusMarkers` (the sparkline complication hardcodes it off).
edge_cases: `now` is captured once via `remember(cgmHistory, config.graphRangeHours)` — the graph does not advance in real time while open; it re-anchors only when the history or range changes.
The Y clamp differs from the sparkline (40/400 vs 20/500), so a reading below 40 or above 400 is clipped off the detail chart but visible on the complication.
No freshness de-emphasis on this screen at all.

capabilities.name: Watch face configuration sync and the phone Settings > Watch UI
capabilities.behavior:
Phone `WatchFaceConfig`: showIoB=true, showGraph=true, showAlert=true, showSeconds=false, graphRangeHours=3 (valid set `listOf(1,3,6)`), theme=Dark, selectedVariant=DIGITAL_FULL, showBasalOverlay/showBolusMarkers/showIoBOverlay/showModeBands=true, aiTtsEnabled=false. Themes: `Dark("Dark","dark")`, `ClinicalBlue("Clinical Blue","clinical_blue")`, `HighContrast("High Contrast","high_contrast")`.

`updateWatchFaceConfig` validates graphRangeHours (fallback 3), persists to `AppSettingsStore` (theme by LABEL, variant by enum NAME — an unknown persisted variant name falls back to DIGITAL_FULL with a warning), and immediately `syncWatchFaceConfig` → `wearDataSender.sendWatchFaceConfig(...)` followed by `wearDataSender.sendCategoryLabels(analyticsSettingsStore.categoryLabels)`. `aiTtsEnabled`/`aiTtsVoice` are always read from the canonical `AppSettingsStore` rather than the config copy, 'to avoid overwriting a value set from the chat screen with a stale snapshot'.

Config is also re-pushed by `checkWatchStatus()` whenever a nearby node with the app is detected (a reconnect re-sync, made deliverable by the `_ts` dedup-buster), and by `AiChatViewModel` on TTS toggle / voice selection.

`checkWatchStatus()`: `CapabilityClient.getCapability("glycemicgpt_watch_app", FILTER_ALL)` inside `withTimeout(WATCH_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000L)`; `watchAppInstalled = capInfo.nodes.isNotEmpty()`, `watchConnected = nearbyNode != null`. Falls back to `NodeClient.connectedNodes` for device NAME and connectivity only — explicitly NOT for `appInstalled`, because NodeClient returns all connected watches. On success it loads the watch version and telemetry.

`loadWatchDataTelemetry()` (`TELEMETRY_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000L`): reads the CGM and IoB DataItems back with `dataUri(...)`, re-applies the `20..500` bound to the cached BG (out-of-range → null), and shows last BG / last IoB with timestamps; failure surfaces `"Could not read watch data"`. All `DataItemBuffer`s are `release()`d.

UI cards (SettingsScreen): `WatchConnectionCard` (status line 'Connected -- streaming BG, IoB, alerts' / 'Installed (not nearby)' / 'Status unknown' + a Check Watch Status button), `WatchFaceGalleryCard` (variant picker + Push button + auto-dismissing Success/Error), `WatchFaceConfigCard` (toggles Show IoB, Show Glucose Graph, **"Alert Vibration"** (=showAlert), Show Seconds; Graph Range 1H/3H/6H chips; Theme radio group; and a Graph Overlays section — Basal Rate Area, Bolus Markers, IoB Overlay, Activity Mode Bands — shown only when `showGraph && selectedVariant.hasGraph`), `WatchAppUpdateCard`, `WatchDataTelemetryCard`. When the app is installed but not nearby: 'Watch app installed but not nearby…'; when not installed: 'Install the GlycemicGPT Wear app on your watch via sideloading…'.
edge_cases: **`cfg_theme` and `cfg_show_seconds` are dead on the watch today**: both are validated and stored in `WatchDataRepository.WatchFaceConfigState` but NOTHING reads them. The WFF faces hardcode their colors and use `format="hh:mm"` with no seconds element. The phone UI still offers a Theme radio group and a Show Seconds toggle.
`cfg_show_bolus` reaches only GraphDetailActivity — the sparkline complication hardcodes bolus markers off.
`cfg_show_alert` is labelled 'Alert Vibration' in the UI and is used solely to gate the watch vibration; it does not hide the Alerts complication.

The architecture doc lists 'Complication slot assignments' and a 'Watch Face Gallery (Future) — preview before pushing' as customization surface; neither is implemented (the gallery card offers variant selection but no preview).

capabilities.name: Wear module manifest, permissions and service registration
capabilities.behavior:
`<uses-feature android:name="android.hardware.type.watch" />`; `<uses-sdk tools:overrideLibrary="androidx.wear.watchface.push" />`.

Permissions: `WAKE_LOCK`, `VIBRATE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, `com.google.wear.permission.PUSH_WATCH_FACES`, `com.google.wear.permission.SET_PUSHED_WATCH_FACE_AS_ACTIVE` (dangerous, requested at runtime), `android.permission.REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES`.
