capabilities.behavior:
docs/mobile/wear-os.md is the user guide. Key facts: the watch face is OPTIONAL — 'the platform and mobile app work without it'. Requires Wear OS 5+; Wear OS 6+ gets phone-side push. Distribution is GitHub Releases only (not Play Store — 'open source diabetes software, not FDA approved').

Wear OS 6+ path: install `wear-device-release.apk` once via ADB, then Settings → Watch → 'Push watch face' in the phone app; the face appears in available faces almost immediately and is activated by long-pressing the current face.
Wear OS 5 path: install BOTH `wear-device-release.apk` and `watchface-release.apk` via ADB; the face is a normal installed APK and the phone cannot push to it.
Updates: Wear OS 6+ re-push from the phone; Wear OS 5 `adb install -r` both APKs.
Developer setup: build number ×7 → Developer Options → ADB debugging + Debug over Wi-Fi; `adb connect <ip>:5555`; target the watch explicitly with `adb -s` when both devices are attached.

Explicit honest notes in the doc: (1) 'The Wear OS install is genuinely the most complicated step in setting up GlycemicGPT. ADB to a watch is a developer-grade workflow.' (2) **'The watch face is read-only. No interactions with it can deliver insulin, change pump settings, or modify your data.'** (3) 'Battery impact on the watch: the face is a normal Wear OS face that updates once per glucose reading interval (~5 minutes). Battery cost is similar to other glucose-monitoring watch faces.' (4) Troubleshooting: if glucose shows `--` for more than 5 minutes after fresh setup — check sign-in and pump/CGM connection, check the Wear OS app shows Connected, and open the phone app once ('it sometimes needs a manual nudge to start forwarding').
edge_cases: The doc's 'Wear OS 5 also install watchface-release.apk' path installs the face with applicationId `com.glycemicgpt.mobile.watchfacepush.glycemicgpt[_mechanical]`, which the WFF template still points at the release wear-device package — correct for release APKs only.

safety_critical: GLUCOSE VALIDITY BOUND 20..500 mg/dL — `GlucoseDisplayUtils.isValidGlucose(mgDl) = mgDl in 20..500`. Enforced at four watch-side points: (1) `GlycemicDataListenerService` CGM_PATH rejects the whole reading; (2) the same service sanitizes an out-of-range `alert_bg` to 0; (3) `BgComplicationDataSource.render` refuses to show an out-of-range value regardless of age; (4) `AlertsActivity` gates the BG line on `bgValue in 20..500` (a raw inline literal). Listed in docs/contract/safety-constants.md as a shipped duplication site covered by the cross-repo drift guard and the CodeRabbit Medical-Safety gate. The phone re-applies it when reading telemetry back (`SettingsViewModel.loadWatchDataTelemetry`). GAP: `GlycemicWearDeviceApp.bootstrapDataFromDataLayer` applies it to the cached CGM but NOT to the cached alert's bgValue.

UNIT CONVERSION FACTOR 18.0156 — `GlucoseDisplayUtils.MGDL_PER_MMOL = 18.0156`, duplicated deliberately from the phone's `GlucoseFormat.MGDL_PER_MMOL` and the backend's `MGDL_PER_MMOL` because the wear module cannot depend on `:app`. Guarded by `SafetyConstantWearGuardTest` (exact equality, delta 0.0) and a cross-surface fixture (54→3.0, 70→3.9, 99→5.5, 100→5.6, 120→6.7, 180→10.0, 250→13.9, 400→22.2). The code comment forbids a second value (18.02 / 18.0182). Conversion divides ONCE and rounds LAST, with `Locale.US` so a comma-decimal locale cannot produce '6,7'. Conversion is DISPLAY-ONLY: the wire value, storage, all threshold comparisons, all color banding, all plotting geometry, and the 20..500 invariant stay canonical mg/dL. `bgColor()` deliberately takes no unit parameter so the user's mmol preference structurally cannot reach the banding decision.

THRESHOLD SANITIZATION ORDERING — `sanitizeThresholds` clamps in a dependent order (`low.coerceIn(40,200)`; `high.coerceIn(max(low+1,100),400)`; `urgentLow.coerceIn(20,low)`; `urgentHigh.coerceIn(high,500)`) so any phone payload — including a corrupt or hostile one — yields `20 ≤ urgentLow ≤ low < high ≤ urgentHigh ≤ 500`. Without this an inverted pair would make `bgColor` mis-band every reading. Defaults when keys are absent: low=70, high=180, urgentLow=55, urgentHigh=250.

STALENESS DETECTION IS TWO INDEPENDENT AXES (GLY-116) AND BOTH MUST FAIL CLOSED. Axis (b) = local aging of shown values against the WATCH's own clock: CGM 6 min STALE / 15 min TOO_STALE; PUMP (IoB) 15 min STALE / 60 min TOO_STALE; half-open boundaries. BG shows the value with a '?' in the STALE band and drops it entirely (rendering '--' while the age keeps counting) at TOO_STALE. IoB does the same on the pump policy — 'an hour-old value presented as current is dosing-relevant misinformation'. Axis (a) = the phone's mirrored coverage claim, which the watch NEVER re-derives and which decays locally after the phone-advertised timeout. The two are deliberately decoupled: BG greys at STALE age even while the mirrored status still says ServerActive. Complication UPDATE_PERIOD_SECONDS=300 on BG/IoB/Alerts exists solely so this decay happens WITHOUT a phone push — a push-only complication would freeze its last reassuring state forever after the phone dies.

BACKWARD WALL-CLOCK JUMP GUARD — `STATUS_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS = 60_000` (mirrors the phone's `ALERT_FLOOR_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS`). Ages more negative than −60 s mean the watch clock jumped backward, which understates EVERY age; both axes fail closed on it (`classify` returns TOO_STALE, `coverageFrom` returns NoRecentStatus, `formatAge` returns 'unknown time' rather than the incoherent 'as of just now — data stale'). Small negative ages are tolerated as routine sampling skew so healthy feeds do not flap.

ALERT DELIVERY GUARANTEES — no delivery receipt anywhere. `WearDataSender` swallows all exceptions with a log line; there is no retry, no queue, no acknowledgement. A vibration fires only when `type != "none" && config.showAlert && rebuzz`; `showAlert=false` (labelled 'Alert Vibration' in phone Settings) silently disables ALL wrist vibration while still updating the display. `rebuzz` defaults to TRUE when the key is absent so an older phone build still buzzes. Sustained alerts re-buzz every `WRIST_ALERT_REBUZZ_MS = 30 min` (= `AlertFloor.FLOOR_COOLDOWN_MS`) and are silently refreshed every `WRIST_ALERT_REFRESH_MS = 5 min` specifically to stay inside the 6-minute CGM STALE band so a still-live alert never greys as 'data stale'.

NEVER RETRACT AN ALERT ON UNTRUSTED DATA — the phone's relay block is entirely skipped when `AlertFloor.isReadingAlertable(reading, nowMs)` is false: no sendAlert, no clearAlert, latch untouched. Documented reason: retracting would flip a possibly-still-true low into the watch's reassuring 'All clear' off data nobody can vouch for. `clearAlert()` is reserved for a genuinely FRESH in-range recovery reading, and is keyed on the server CLASSIFICATION being null rather than on the watch-type mapping being null (a mapping gap must cost a push, never produce an 'All clear').

'ALL CLEAR' IS RESERVED FOR A CURRENT WATCHING CLAIM — `AlertsActivity.NoAlertContent` shows the green 'All clear' ONLY for `WristCoverage.Watching`; `NotWatching` and `NoRecentStatus` each render explicit degraded copy. `AlertsComplicationDataSource` mirrors this: the quiet grey bell requires `covered`, everything else is amber. The stale-alert grey is deliberately gated on `covered` too — 'a real alert whose phone then dies ages past the cap and never auto-clears, and quiet grey there would be indistinguishable from the healthy all-clear, suppressing the dead-phone cue in exactly the case it exists for.'

MONITORING-STATUS DECAY MUST NOT BE DEFEATED BY A CORRUPT PAYLOAD — the watch clamps the phone-advertised timeout to `10_000L .. 1_800_000L` (floor covers the 20 s compressed debug policy; cap stops a dead phone's last 'watching' surviving for hours) and rejects any `mon_state` outside the three known values. Monitoring status is deliberately NOT persisted across a watch process restart — coverage after a restart is genuinely unknown and the fail-closed render is the honest one. Unknown state strings fail closed to NoRecentStatus.

HEARTBEAT IS THE DEAD-PHONE DETECTOR — `WearMonitoringStatusForwarder` re-sends on a heartbeat of `max(timeoutMs/2, 5_000)` (3 min in production) as well as on change, because the source flow deduplicates and a healthy steady state would emit once, leaving a disconnected watch holding a frozen 'watching' forever. The `_ts` dedup-buster in the DataMap is what makes the unchanged heartbeat actually deliverable. `retryWhen` with a 5 s delay resubscribes on stream failure — 'a coverage-status stream must never die silently.'

INSULIN/DOSING DISPLAY BOUNDS — history overlay records are filtered at receipt against Tandem pump safety limits: `MAX_BOLUS_UNITS = 25f` (max single bolus) applied to `units`, `correctionUnits` AND `mealUnits`; `MAX_BASAL_RATE = 15f` U/hr; `iob >= 0f`; all require `timestampMs > 0`. `MAX_HISTORY_RECORDS = 500` per type. The decoder additionally guards against Int overflow when computing required bytes (`count.toLong() * recordSize.toLong()`). Live IoB (`IOB_PATH`) is NOT range-validated — only aged. The watch face is documented as strictly read-only: no interaction can deliver insulin, change pump settings, or modify data.

REASON-CODE VOCABULARY IS A LOAD-BEARING CONTRACT — the five `MONITORING_REASON_*` constants must match the phone's `FloorNotWatchingReason` enum names exactly; a rename would silently degrade the watch to generic copy. `AlertsCopyTest` pins every arm to a distinct line, described as 'the wear analogue of the store's silent-disarm', which is why `notWatchingReasonCopy` is `internal` rather than `private`.

WFF PROVIDER PACKAGE MUST TRACK THE BUILD TYPE — `GenerateWatchFaceXmlTask` throws a GradleException if the template lacks the `@WEAR_PKG@` token, because a hardcoded package would leave RELEASE faces pointing complications at the DEBUG wear app, producing a face with permanently dead glucose/IoB/graph slots on a fresh production install. Backed by `WatchFacePusherTest` assertions that release assets never reference the debug wear package.

PUSHED APK INTEGRITY — the phone verifies the bundled WFF asset's SHA-256 against a `BuildConfig` value Gradle computes from the same committed file at build time (so the runtime tamper check is always in lockstep), and refuses to push on mismatch. The watch validates the received file's PK zip magic bytes, caps it at 50 MB (100 MB for the wear APK), and requires a non-empty DWF validation token before calling `addWatchFace`/`updateWatchFace`. `committed-assets.sha256` plus the JVM drift gate prevent a hand-edited or partially regenerated asset from shipping.

APPLICATION-ID EQUALITY IS A SILENT-FAILURE HAZARD — if `:wear-device`'s applicationId ever diverges from `:app`'s, the Data Layer drops every message and DataItem with no error surfaced to the user; the watch would keep rendering its last cached (reassuring) values until they age out. Discovered the hard way in Story 32.8.

map.notes:
GAPS AND DEAD PATHS FOUND IN THE CURRENT CODE (all verified by reading, not inferred):

1. Install/update status messages are write-only. The watch sends `status=...` payloads on `/glycemicgpt/watchface/status` and `/glycemicgpt/watch/apk/status` to every connected node, but the phone manifest registers MESSAGE_RECEIVED only for `/glycemicgpt/chat/` and the exact path `/glycemicgpt/alert/dismiss`, and no phone source file references either status path. Consequences: `WatchFacePusher.Result.Success("sent")` means only 'bytes transferred' (its own KDoc says so, referencing an unimplemented Story 32.4), and `WatchAppUpdateState.Installing → Success` is driven by a bare `delay(15_000L)` timer. A validation failure, a denied SET_PUSHED_WATCH_FACE_AS_ACTIVE, or a failed PackageInstaller commit all still show the user a success state.

2. `cfg_theme` and `cfg_show_seconds` are inert on the watch. Both are transmitted, validated (`VALID_THEMES`, default "dark"; showSeconds default false) and stored in `WatchFaceConfigState`, but no watch code reads them — grep confirms zero consumers outside the contract/repository/listener. The WFF faces hardcode all colors and use `format="hh:mm"` with no seconds element. The phone Settings UI nevertheless presents a three-option Theme radio group and a Show Seconds toggle.

3. `BolusHistoryRecord.category` is always the empty string — the 21-byte wire record carries no category field and the decoder never populates it — so the `categoryLabels[record.category]` lookup in `GraphDetailActivity.buildBolusLabel` is dead unless the phone sends a map containing an empty-string key. Category labels are otherwise transmitted and stored correctly.

4. `IoBComplicationDataSource` is the only data-reading complication that does NOT call `WatchDataRepository.init(applicationContext)`; the other three added it explicitly (the Alerts one after a bug). A cold complication-only process can therefore render `--` for IoB while BG and the graph render restored data.

5. `GlycemicWearDeviceApp.bootstrapDataFromDataLayer` replays the cached alert WITHOUT running `alert_bg` through `isValidGlucose` (the live listener does), so a corrupt cached alert can restore an out-of-range bgValue into the repository. `AlertsActivity`'s own `bgValue in 20..500` gate is the backstop.

6. The three oldest `WearDataSender` methods (`sendIoB`, `sendCgm`, `sendAlert`) catch bare `Exception` and therefore swallow `CancellationException`; the newer methods rethrow it first.

7. The graph surfaces use two DIFFERENT Y clamps: the sparkline complication clamps to 20..500, the full-screen detail view to 40..400 (`Y_MIN_DEFAULT`/`Y_MAX_DEFAULT`). A reading below 40 or above 400 is visible on the complication but clipped off the detail chart. Neither graph surface applies any freshness de-emphasis.

8. The wrist dismiss does not clear the phone's `previousAlertType` latch, so an ongoing episode re-pushes (and re-buzzes on the 30-minute cadence) after a dismiss.

9. Watch-side chat timeout (30 s) is materially shorter than the phone-side API timeout (90 s); a late response can replace a displayed timeout error with a Success state.

DOCUMENTED DELIBERATE DECISIONS worth carrying into any port: no separate wear companion phone app (rejected with five stated reasons); the wear module deliberately has NO dependency on `:app`, so `WearDataContract`, `WearHistorySerializer`, `GlucoseUnit` and the freshness tiers are hand-mirrored with `// MIRROR:` headers and contract tests instead of shared code; monitoring status is deliberately not persisted; the alert-relay skip on non-alertable readings is deliberate (never retract on untrusted data); the EPL-1.0 xpath2 processor exclusion is a license decision protected by an instrumented test; the classes.dex strip + v1-JAR re-sign is required because the DwfValidator rejects dex and requires v1 signing; the Samsung Wear OS 6 double-update is a workaround for DefaultProviderPolicy evaluation ordering; the `_ts` DataMap key is a workaround for Data Layer deduplication and is load-bearing for the coverage heartbeat.

port.subsystem: Wear OS watch face and companion → Apple Watch (watchOS) app, WidgetKit complications, and the iPhone↔Watch bridge

ports_cleanly.capability: Architecture: single phone app + watch-side code, no separate companion phone app (docs/dev/wear-os-architecture.md:12-20 rejected the companion app)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: One Xcode project, three-plus targets: iOS app, watchOS app (single-target watchOS app, watchOS 7+ style), iOS widget extension, watchOS widget extension. Apple enforces the pairing the Android team had to enforce by hand: the watchOS app bundle ID must be `<iOSBundleID>.watchkitapp` with `WKCompanionAppBundleIdentifier` pointing at the iOS app. The Android `applicationId` equality hazard (Story 32.8 silent Data Layer drops) has an exact iOS analogue — a mismatched `WKCompanionAppBundleIdentifier` yields a watch app that installs but whose `WCSession` never pairs, with no user-visible error — so it must be pinned by a build-time check the same way. The `:watchface` module disappears entirely (see impossible). Shared logic moves into a Swift Package (`GlycemicCore`) linked by all four targets, which is strictly better than Android's hand-mirrored `// MIRROR:` copies.

ports_cleanly.capability: Watch freshness policy (WatchFreshness): CGM 6/15 min, PUMP 15/60 min, half-open boundaries, −60 s backward-clock guard, DEFAULT_STATUS_TIMEOUT_MS
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure value logic — port verbatim into `GlycemicCore` as a Swift enum + free functions and link it into the iOS app, watch app, and BOTH widget extensions. Because SPM lets the watch genuinely share code with the phone, the entire `// MIRROR:` drift class the Android module lives with is eliminated inside the app; the mirrored-constant tests survive only as cross-repo pins against the backend and web. Use `Date.timeIntervalSince` in seconds or keep milliseconds as `Int64` — keep milliseconds to preserve the exact test fixtures (6min−1ms FRESH / 6min STALE etc.). ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct port into `GlycemicCore`. `mgDl.coerceIn(a,b)` → `min(max(v,a),b)` or `v.clamped(to: a...b)`; keep the exact dependent clamp ORDER so the invariant 20 ≤ urgentLow ≤ low < high ≤ urgentHigh ≤ 500 still holds for hostile input. `String.format(Locale.US, "%.1f", …)` → `String(format: "%.1f", …)` is locale-dependent in Swift too, so it MUST be `String(format:locale:)` with `Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")`, otherwise a comma-decimal locale reproduces the exact bug the Kotlin `Locale.US` was guarding. Keep `bgColor` free of any unit parameter so the mmol preference structurally cannot reach the banding decision. Port the cross-surface fixture (54→3.0 … 400→22.2) as an XCTest. ports_cleanly.capability: Watch-side state store (WatchDataRepository): StateFlows, 72-entry CGM ring buffer with 30 s dedup window, SharedPreferences cache of CGM history / current CGM / current IoB / glucose unit, monitoring status deliberately NOT persisted, coverageFrom() decay decision
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: An `actor` (or `@Observable` final class on the main actor) in the watch app, backed by a shared App Group container (`group.<id>.watch`) so the watchOS widget extension — a SEPARATE process — can read the same cache.
